Reads incoming SMS and forwards them to your own server endpoint. The app stays deliberately thin: it does not talk to Telegram or email directly — it just POSTs each SMS as JSON to your primary endpoint, falling back to a backup endpoint if the primary fails. Your server decides where to relay it (Telegram, email, or anything else), so adding channels never requires rebuilding the app.

Capture: a real-time SMS broadcast receiver (works even when the app process has been killed — the system relaunches it to deliver the broadcast), plus an optional periodic reconciliation that re-sends anything missed.

Forwarding: fully decoupled from capture. Each message is queued to WorkManager with exponential-backoff retries that survive process death and reboot.

Survival: a persistent foreground service, auto-restart on boot, battery-optimization exemption, and OEM auto-start whitelisting keep it running long-term.

For personal use. Not published to any app store.
